newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Pfizer Q4 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Pfizer Q4 earnings.

text.p: Pfizer issued the following release on its 1996 Q4 and annual earnings.
Pfizer Inc Fourth-Quarter Sales Grew 15 Percent;
Net Income Increased 23 Percent
Earnings per share rose by 18 percent for the quarter,
20 percent for the year

NEW YORK, Jan. 16 /PRNewswire/ -- Pfizer Inc today reported that for the fourth quarter of 1996 sales increased by 15 percent to $3,160 million and net income increased by 23 percent to $504 million. Earnings per share were 77 cents, an increase of 18 percent.

Sales for the full year reached $11,306 million, an increase of 13 percent, while net income grew by 23 percent, reaching $1,929 million. On a per share basis, earnings were $2.99, an increase of 20 percent. Eliminating the impact of foreign exchange, sales increased by 17 percent for the quarter and 15 percent for the year, with growth essentially all volume-driven.

"As a company, we are entering an era of unprecedented new-product opportunity," said William C. Steere, Jr., chairman and chief executive officer. "We will be launching two major new human pharmaceuticals early this year plus several new indications for existing products. We filed a new drug application in December for Trovan, our broad-spectrum quinolone antibiotic and, based on the extensive and compelling nature of the application, we hope to be able to launch this exciting product by the end of the year or in early 1998. Moreover, the depth and quality of our research pipeline promises a steady stream of major new products throughout the rest of the century and beyond."

The imminent new product launches are Aricept, a treatment for Alzheimer's disease patients, and Lipitor(TM) (atorvastatin calcium), for -- the treatment of elevated blood-cholesterol levels. Aricept was discovered and developed by Eisai Co., Ltd.; Lipitor was discovered and developed by Warner-Lambert Company. Both products received U.S. marketing clearance during the past two months. In addition, regulators in the United Kingdom and in Germany have given marketing clearance to Lipitor. Pfizer will co-promote or co-market these exciting new products with Eisai and Warner-Lambert respectively.

"Heightened levels of investments are needed to participate in the launches of these major new products and support the necessary post-launch clinical research and development. However, we believe the commercial opportunity these products present is compelling," Mr. Steere said. "Furthermore, we anticipate an increase of about 20 percent in R&D spending for 1997 -- to approximately $2 billion -- to continue our important discovery work and to develop the significant number of late-stage clinical candidates in our R&D pipeline. In spite of this substantial investment to support the near-, mid- and long-term success of Pfizer, we expect to achieve double-digit growth in both sales and net income this year."
Fourth-Quarter Sales by Segment
Health Care segment sales increased by 18 percent, driven by sales growth of 20 percent in Pharmaceuticals (28 percent in the U.S. and 10 percent internationally) and 8 percent in Hospital Products.

In Pharmaceuticals, cardiovascular product sales continued to grow strongly. Sales of Norvasc, our intrinsically once-a-day treatment for hypertension and angina and the company's largest-selling product, increased by 41 percent to $516 million. Sales of Procardia XL, for the treatment of hypertension and angina, declined by 6 percent to $255 million, partially reflecting the company's increasing emphasis on Norvasc. Norvasc has recently been found safe to treat both angina and hypertension in patients with congestive heart failure. Sales of Cardura, a drug for the treatment of hypertension and enlarged prostate, increased by 31 percent to $150 million. The increase was partially driven by additional international approvals for the prostate indication, known medically as benign prostatic hyperplasia.

Zoloft sales increased by 31 percent to $372 million. Zoloft is a leader among the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, the fastest-growing class of anti-depressants. In October Zoloft was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder.

Sales of Diflucan, a treatment for fungal infections, increased by 4 percent to $240 million. Diflucan has a large percentage of its sales in Japan, and thus was disproportionately affected by the weakness of the yen relative to the dollar. Excluding the effects of foreign exchange, sales increased by 7 percent. Diflucan is the world's largest-selling prescription anti-fungal product.

Zithromax sales increased by 44 percent to $199 million, partially as a result of the additional approvals of this antibiotic for the prevention of Mycobacterium avium complex in advanced HIV-positive patients and treatment of middle-ear and strep throat infections in children. A relatively severe season for flu and associated respiratory infections in the U.S. also contributed to increased demand for Zithromax.
Sales of Zyrtec, our allergy medication launched in the U.S. in January 1996, were $49 million. In November, Pfizer launched a new syrup formulation for children 6 to 11 years of age.

The increase of sales for Hospital Products was fueled by the acquisition of the Leibinger Companies in January 1996 and the demand for stents. The Leibinger Companies are leaders in the manufacture of implantable devices and specialty surgical instruments.

Sales of stents -- devices used to maintain flow through obstructed esophageal, urological, coronary and other vessels -- increased by 45 percent to $31 million. This performance reflects the launches of two new stent products. For the year, stent sales -- worldwide for esophageal and urological applications and internationally for coronary use -- exceeded $100 million.

Animal Health results continue to reflect adverse market conditions, particularly in food animals in the U.S. Sales of the segment increased by 1 percent worldwide, reflecting a 7-percent decline in the U.S. for the quarter. Sales of Dectomax, the antiparasitic for livestock which is -- the business' leading product, increased by 46 percent to $33 million. Sales of Stafac, a leading antibacterial for poultry and swine, increased by 18 percent to $23 million. This month, Pfizer Animal Health launched Rimadyl, a prescription treatment for pain and inflammation in dogs, in the U.S.

Consumer Health sales increased by 10 percent for the quarter, driven by growth from key in-line products and two acquired brands: Cortizone, the leading topical over-the-counter anti-itch treatment in the U.S., and Hemorid, an OTC treatment for hemorrhoids.

"We are approaching the commercialization of our next wave of innovative human pharmaceutical products," said David Shedlarz, senior vice president and chief financial officer, "which we expect to sustain our strong sales momentum. In order to fully realize the potential of our near-term product opportunities, we plan heightened investments in marketing, sales and research. Our 1997 earnings will depend heavily on the size and timing of these investments and the performance of new products."

"The challenge at hand for Pfizer is managing our large number of opportunities: striking the right balance between sustained growth and investment," said Mr. Steere. "Fortunately, the success of our existing products, strong commercial potential of new products and improved organizational efficiency and effectiveness position us well to meet this challenge. We believe our investments will return benefits in both the short term, and for many years to come."

Forward-looking statements in this document should be evaluated with due consideration given the many uncertainties inherent in our business, particularly those mentioned in the cautionary statements in Exhibit 99 of our 1995 Form 10-K, which we incorporate here by reference. SOURCE Pfizer Inc
